title: Pointing at a turning point parked on a corner shows the grab hand again
goal: When a layer's turning point is dragged onto one of its corners, pointing at that spot should show the hand that says you can grab the turning point. Since some change on 2026-09-28 or 2026-09-29, the pointer shows nothing there at all, so a person cannot tell which of the two marks on that spot a press would take.
notes: Found by the rotating check at 2026-09-29T11:03:34Z. No task owned it, because no standing walk task was open (see the loop task filed alongside this one). Reproduced by the daily digest on 2026-09-29 at 87071807 with the probe built at 05:10: `Scripts/playtest-all.sh --no-build motion-pivot-in-a-corner` -> `motion-pivot-in-a-corner-walk 7s FAILED step 24 (expectCue): the canvas says a press here would be "none", not "grab"`. Its log at step 21 says `move to (420, 230) document = view (448, 262); nothing under the pointer watches for one`, so the pointer is not reaching whatever watches the canvas at that point. Last pass seen in the loop log: the rotating check around 2026-09-28T21:11Z. Between the two: the floating tool bar spacing and height (98f6c6f5, 3e3bafea), the canvas foot layout (dd15d5fe), the dropdown rebuild (e121747f), the segmented control (8e594bb1) and the timeline outline and resize edge (2c6b55bd). Start by running the walk at each of those.
acceptance: The task log names the change that broke it and why the pointer stopped reacting over that spot
Other walks that check what the pointer says over the canvas still pass (Scripts/playtest-all.sh --no-build expectCue is not a name, so run the motion and cursor walks)

Restored stash ad0f63cc (previous attempt's harness fix). At HEAD a96b4e54 without it the walk passed 6/6 with the person's pointer at the screen edge (1728,987), so no commit broke it; the previous attempt also saw it fail at c489684d, older than every suspect.

Cause: every canvas update (CanvasDisplay.apply -> refreshGrabCursor()) re-reads the cue with no event, falling back to window.mouseLocationOutsideOfEventStream = the PERSON's real pointer, not the walk's synthesized one. Outside the canvas bounds that path returns without recording, so the reading stays grab (pass); when the real pointer rests over the probe's canvas area (even with the probe buried under other windows) it records 'none' (fail). Not an app bug: for a person the real pointer is the pointer and the cue is right.

Reproduced deterministically (person idle 3h): CGWarpMouseCursorPosition to (300,350) over the probe canvas, then Scripts/playtest.sh Scripts/playtest/motion-pivot-in-a-corner-walk.json --no-build -> FAILED step 24 (expectCue): "none", not "grab"; same for a scratch walk that nudges+undoes to force a refresh. Pointer put back at (1727,987).

Fix 17daae0b: PlaytestPointer remembers where the walk last put the pointer (every synthesized mouse event and rest); CanvasNSView.restingPointer() reads that during a walk. With the pointer parked over the canvas: pivot walk + scratch walk 5/5 ok. Cue walks (crop-cue, grab-cue, motion-path, notice-waits-under-the-pointer, pen-two-points, screen-drag-cue) 7/7 ok; all 10 motion walks ok. Scripts/test.sh: 10561 tests passed.
